children: 5N Plus has been awarded $7.3 million by the U.S. Department of War to establish domestic production of gallium arsenide components for U.S. defense applications.

Gallium arsenide is a strategically important semiconductor material used in advanced sensing systems and other devices for defense applications, but the U.S. currently doesn't have a qualified domestic source, forcing defense contractors to rely on foreign suppliers.

The Montreal-based producer of specialty semiconductors and performance materials said Thursday that the proposed award would help to establish a qualified U.S. source at its production facility in St. George, Utah, and help address the supply chain gap.

"This award will enable us to establish a secure domestic source for an immediate defense requirement, while also creating a scalable platform to pursue significant long-term market opportunities across a broader range of defense and space applications," Chief Executive Officer Richard Perron said.
